description: Figure 19 is a grouped vertical bar chart illustrating the average probing accuracy difference (in percentage points) for two multilingual BERT models across several MLP probe variations, with hidden-layer sizes shown in square brackets. The horizontal axis contains four categorical MLP configurations ordered left to right as “hidden:[50], linear,” “hidden:[1], linear,” “hidden:[100], ReLU,” and “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU.” The vertical axis is labeled “% point difference” and uses a linear scale spanning approximately from −0.2 to +0.2, with regularly spaced tick marks at about 0.1 intervals (−0.2, −0.1, 0, 0.1, 0.2). Each category has two adjacent bars identified by the legend: mBERT is shown in a light blue bar and XLM-R is shown in a darker blue bar. For “hidden:[50], linear,” the mBERT bar is around −0.15 and the XLM-R bar is around −0.05; for “hidden:[1], linear,” mBERT is about +0.09 and XLM-R is about +0.21; for “hidden:[100], ReLU,” mBERT is about −0.11 and XLM-R is about +0.02; and for “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU,” mBERT is about −0.15 and XLM-R is about −0.12. The bars are not visually annotated beyond the legend and axis labels, and there is no indication that the categories are sorted by value.
